coverage_note: 10:00-14:02 Medi on a work phone call (English only); 19:58-23:14 Amal disconnected. 17:00-31:00 and 49:00-1:00:00 much Arabic is Latin-transliterated by the engine (Shantet Shogoli, awal usbu'a, laffe). Engine: 'divine' at 01:33 = الزباين (Amal's echo); الأواى / هوايحة at 34:48/37:16 = أواعيها; هذا at 46:00-46:37 is the engine for حدا (Amal says الحدا/حدا back). 04:14 'لازم air conditioning': Amal only asked 'لازم إيش؟' and gave no verb - no B2 slip (GR-27); air conditioning not on her sheet. No echo-candidates file exists for 2026-10-01. Most of the lesson is English-language grammar discussion (idafa/el- placement, awal/nafs/gher), so few free-speech turns.

rows.amal_said: شو يعني لسه الزباين يروحوا؟ ... لا، لا الزباين يروحوا. ... There are other words, but the one we know is لا.
rows.why: He used لسه (still/yet) for 'until'; Amal asked what he meant and gave la- (la ezzbaayen yroo7u). Engine wrote 'divine' for الزباين (her echo).

rows.amal_said: واحد. ... أول شي what's the [day] then the date.
rows.chat: yoam el-5amees, wa7ad 3ashara alafain u sitte u 3eshreen
rows.why: For the date (1st) he said the feminine واحدة; Amal said واحد and her chat writes wa7ad 3ashara.
Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal echoed his واحد, he caught it ('times are واحدة') and she confirmed الساعة واحدة.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، uh، أخ-أخ-أخضر أو،
rows.why: Feminine noun بلوزة needs the feminine colour; Amal prompted 'بلوزة شو؟' and he fixed to خضرا ('it's feminine').

rows.amal_said: Hafiz is a motivation، بس what's about motivated؟ ... متشـ... متشجع.
rows.why: Asked for yesterday's word 'motivated' he gave حافز (sheet: 'motivation | 7aafez daafe3'); Amal said that's motivation and supplied متشجع (sheet: 'motivated | Mitshajje3'). Engine wrote حافظ.
He repeats مشجع (fan/encourager) for her متشجع (motivated, sheet 'Mitshajje3'); at 07:47 she starts 'مت--' to fix it. One row, first occurrence.

rows.medi_said: Is there a verb for حساب? Do you guys use it?
rows.why: He asked for the verb 'to consider'; Amal supplied بحسب - a didn't-know.
Amal's question uses متشجع + la- (إله); he dropped the preposition and she did not fix it.

rows.medi_said: أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.amal_said: Yeah I'm on the wifi أنا عالـ wifi.
rows.why: 'On the wifi' takes على not في; he asked and Amal gave أنا عالـ wifi.
He dropped el- after على; Amal repeated 'على الـ، عالـ'.

rows.medi_said: So Shanteti, ... El Shogolelah El, uh, Amra.
rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: In idafa the owner ending goes on the last noun; Amal made him build 'work bag' first and he said 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'.

rows.amal_said: That would mean is red. ... the adjective after it should be definitive as well.
rows.why: A definite (possessed) noun needs el- on its adjective; Amal said without it it means 'is red' and explained the rule.
شنتة is feminine so the colour is الحمرا; Amal recast and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: Not here. ... ما فيهن means there aren't here or there isn't here.
rows.why: 'Not here' negates an adverb with مش; ما فيه = there isn't. Amal explained and he produced مش هون, she confirmed 'مشون'.
اسم is masculine and takes no -t in idafa; Amal said 'ليش؟ لا' and 'It's just اسم'.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; she let it pass (the الـ may be a hesitation).
The first word of idafa never takes el-; Amal said لا twice (29:57, 30:21).
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة.
rows.amal_said: لا. لا. You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: For 'the old name' the adjective must agree with اسم (masculine); Amal said لا and 'change the gender of 2adeem'.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.why: He left out 'her'; Amal prompted 'But her' and he later built محل أواعيها المفضل (engine wrote الأواى).
طيارة is feminine; Amal offered متأخر أو متأخرة, he chose المتأخرة and she asked why (طيارة).

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we [say] the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: Superlative + noun takes no el-; Amal said No and named the rule.

rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل is like more efficient.
rows.why: محل is masculine so هذا, not هذي; Amal accepted it and only offered هذا أحسن محل.

rows.medi_said: أس-- أسوأ الزبون. ... أسوأ الزبون. ... أحسن الزبون
rows.why: Same rule just taught at 41:23 (no el- after a superlative); he said it three times and Amal never voiced it - only her chat wrote aswa2 zboon.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن الزبون ما، ما تشتري إشي.
rows.why: The sentence is 'the worst customer is the one who doesn't buy'; he said أحسن (best) for أسوأ (worst) - her chat has aswa2.
rows.english: the worst customer doesn't buy anything

rows.medi_said: ما تشتري إشي. ما بتشتري. ما بتشتري.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: زبون is masculine so the verb is بيشتري; Amal recast and said why, he repeated ما بيشتري.
Fronted object needs the pointer ending; Amal said بحبه and he said 'There's a pointer'.
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal is the first exercise.
rows.why: Amal taught that awal before a noun never takes el-; he put el- on it and she only acknowledged the second form.
rows.proposed_rule: awal / akher / tani before a noun never take el-: awal sayyaara = the first car (after the noun as an adjective: el-laffe el-oola)

rows.amal_said: Al laffa al oola. ... Al laffa, what does al laffa mean?
rows.chat: awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola
rows.why: Repeating her phrase he dropped el- on laffe; she repeated 'Al laffa al oola' until he got it.

rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: Amal recast nafs ishi to nafs el-ishi and said the version without el- means nothing.
rows.proposed_rule: After nafs (same) the noun takes el-: nafs el-ishi = the same thing (nafs ishi is wrong)
